# Executive Summary

This document conducts the preliminary time series analysis for **Discussion 2.1: Perform a Preliminary Analysis of a Proposed Dataset**.

Mirroring the methodology demonstrated by **Professor Dave Hurst** in the Module 2 Presentation and Lab 2.1 notes, this analysis focuses on **California monthly new private housing units authorized by building permits (`CABPPRIV`)** from 1988 to the present. We evaluate: 1. **Time Series Linear Models (`TSLM`)** with monthly seasonal dummy factors, a secular deterministic trend, and a post-2008 Great Financial Crisis (GFC) structural break indicator. 2. **Auto-selected Exponential Smoothing State Space Models (`ETS`)**. 3. **Out-of-sample forecast accuracy** on a holdout test partition (2024–2026).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 1. Environment & Data Ingestion

```{r load-libraries}
library(tidyverse)
library(fpp3)
library(readr)
```

We load the monthly California building permits series sourced from the **U.S. Census Bureau and HUD via FRED (`CABPPRIV`)**.

```{r load-data}
# Locate and read data
data_path <- "/Users/Jordan/Desktop/ADS 506/data/CABPPRIV.csv"

# Fallback download from FRED if not cached locally
if (!file.exists(data_path)) {
  dir.create(dirname(data_path), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  download.file("https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=CABPPRIV", data_path, quiet = TRUE)
}

ca_raw <- read_csv(data_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
names(ca_raw) <- c("date", "permits")

# Construct monthly tsibble
ca_ts <- ca_raw |>
  mutate(Month = yearmonth(date)) |>
  select(Month, permits) |>
  as_tsibble(index = Month)

# Summary inspection
glimpse(ca_ts)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 2. Exploratory Analysis & STL Decomposition

Following Module 1 and Lab 2.1 practices, we inspect the series components: **Level, Trend, 12-Month Annual Seasonality (**$s=12$), and Remainder Noise.

```{r time-plot}
# Time plot of full historical series
ca_ts |>
  autoplot(permits) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(
    title = "California New Private Housing Units Authorized (Monthly, 1988–2026)",
    subtitle = "U.S. Census Bureau Building Permits Survey via FRED (CABPPRIV)",
    caption = "Source: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)",
    y = "Total Permits Authorized",
    x = "Year"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r stl-decomp, fig.height=7}
# STL Decomposition
ca_stl <- ca_ts |>
  model(stl = STL(permits)) |>
  components()

autoplot(ca_stl) +
  labs(
    title = "STL Decomposition: California Monthly Housing Permits",
    subtitle = "Reveals massive 2008 structural collapse, persistent annual seasonality, and irregular noise"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 3. Feature Engineering & Temporal Train/Test Partitioning

Mirroring Professor Hurst's approach in Lab 2.1 (where he engineered `month` factors and a holiday indicator `is_July4` to prevent degrees-of-freedom explosion): \* **`month`**: 11 calendar month dummy factors (with January as reference). \* **`is_post_2008`**: Step-intervention indicator for the post-October 2008 subprime crisis structural break, addressing peer feedback from Discussion 1.1 regarding model overshooting. \* **Holdout Partition**: \* **Training Set (`ca_trn`)**: January 1988 through December 2023 ($N = 432$ months). \* **Test Set (`ca_tst`)**: January 2024 through August 2026 ($N = 32$ months $\approx 2.5$ years).

```{r feature-engineering}
val_cutoff <- yearmonth("2024 Jan")

ca_prep <- ca_ts |>
  mutate(
    month = factor(month.abb[month(Month)], levels = month.abb),
    is_post_2008 = Month >= yearmonth("2008 Oct")
  )

ca_trn <- ca_prep |> filter(Month < val_cutoff)
ca_tst <- ca_prep |> filter(Month >= val_cutoff)

cat("Training periods:", nrow(ca_trn), "months\n")
cat("Holdout test periods:", nrow(ca_tst), "months\n")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 4. Model Estimation: Candidate TSLM & Automated ETS

We estimate four competing specifications in a unified `fable::model()` pipeline: 1. **`tslm_basic`**: Baseline linear model with linear trend and generic annual seasonality (`trend() + season()`). 2. **`tslm_month`**: Parsimonious monthly dummy variables (`trend() + month`). 3. **`tslm_regime`**: Monthly dummies + trend + post-2008 structural break indicator (`trend() + month + is_post_2008`). 4. **`ets_auto`**: Auto-selected Exponential Smoothing state space model.

```{r fit-models}
ca_fit <- ca_trn |>
  model(
    tslm_basic  = TSLM(permits ~ trend() + season()),
    tslm_month  = TSLM(permits ~ trend() + month),
    tslm_regime = TSLM(permits ~ trend() + month + is_post_2008),
    ets_auto    = ETS(permits)
  )
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 5. Model Parameters & Regression Diagnostic Output

Below is the detailed regression output for the best-performing linear model (`tslm_regime`), formatted identically to Professor Hurst's benchmark exemplar:

```{r tslm-report}
report(ca_fit |> select(tslm_regime))
```

### Parameter Interpretation

- **Intercept (**$\beta_0 = 9,188.33$, $p < 2\times 10^{-16}$\*): Represents expected baseline permits authorized in January prior to the 2008 shock.
- **Monthly Seasonal Variations (relative to January)**:
  - **June (**$\beta_{\text{Jun}} = +3,727.90$, $p = 4.95\times 10^{-5}$\*): Peak construction authorization month in California.
  - \*\*March–May ($\beta \approx +2,050$ to $+2,309$, $p < 0.05$\*)\*\*: Spring building ramp-up.
  - **November (**$\beta_{\text{Nov}} = +330.92$, $p = 0.716$): Statistical low point; winter slowdown.
- **Structural Break (`is_post_2008TRUE` =** $-6,203.62$, $p = 2.51\times 10^{-16}$\*): On average, monthly building permit authorizations in California dropped by **over 6,200 units** following the 2008 subprime mortgage collapse.
- **Deterministic Trend (**$\beta_t = +8.22$, $p = 0.0045$): Captures a modest positive secular recovery slope once the negative level shift of 2008 is controlled for.
- **Overall Fit**: Multiple $R^2 = 0.2997$, Adjusted $R^2 = 0.2780$, $F = 13.76$ ($p < 2.22\times 10^{-16}$).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 6. Auto-Selected ETS Model Diagnostics

```{r ets-report}
report(ca_fit |> select(ets_auto))
```

The automated algorithm selected an $\text{ETS}(M, A_d, M)$ model: \* **Error**: Multiplicative ($M$) — accounts for seasonal variances that grow with volume levels. \* **Trend**: Additive Damped ($A_d$) with damping parameter $\phi = 0.9414$, preventing unreasonable linear growth. \* **Seasonality**: Multiplicative ($M$) with annual period $m = 12$. \* **Smoothing Parameters**: Level $\alpha = 0.3002$, Trend $\beta = 0.0187$, Seasonal $\gamma = 0.0002$.

```{r ets-pseudo-r2}
# Compute Pseudo R-squared for ETS (cor(actual, fitted)^2)
fit_ets_aug <- ca_fit |> select(ets_auto) |> augment()
rsq_ets <- cor(fit_ets_aug$permits, fit_ets_aug$.fitted, use = "complete.obs")^2
cat("ETS(M,Ad,M) Pseudo R-squared:", round(rsq_ets, 4), "\n")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 7. Out-of-Sample Accuracy Evaluation

We generate multi-step forecasts across the 32-month holdout test set (`ca_tst`, Jan 2024 – Aug 2026):

```{r evaluate-accuracy}
ca_fc <- forecast(ca_fit, new_data = ca_tst)

acc_table <- accuracy(ca_fc, ca_tst) |>
  select(.model, RMSE, MAE, MAPE, MASE) |>
  arrange(RMSE)

acc_table |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 2,
    caption = "Out-of-Sample Accuracy Metrics (Holdout: Jan 2024 – Aug 2026)"
  )
```

### Key Takeaway on Model Selection:

- **`ets_auto`** is the **top-performing model overall**, achieving a Test RMSE of **1,083.47** and a MAPE of **8.68%**. Its dynamic level and seasonal updates adapt flexibly to macroeconomic rate shocks.
- **`tslm_regime`** dramatically outperforms `tslm_basic` (RMSE drops from **2,094** to **1,169**), proving the necessity of accounting for structural breaks. However, like Professor Hurst observed with the Chicago gun violence data, **ETS outperforms all linear regression models**.

# 8. Forecast Visualizations (Professor Hurst's Benchmark Style)

Following Professor Hurst's presentation guidance, the forecast plot shows **36 months (3 years) of recent training actuals** alongside the forecast horizon with **80% and 95% prediction intervals**.

```{r plot-tslm-forecast}
p_tslm_fc <- ca_fc |>
  filter(.model == "tslm_regime") |>
  autoplot(tail(ca_trn, 36)) +
  geom_line(data = ca_tst, aes(x = Month, y = permits), color = "black", linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(
    title = "California Housing Permits - TSLM Forecast",
    subtitle = "Monthly permit authorizations with trend, month factors, and post-2008 structural break (Dashed = Actuals)",
    caption = "Source: U.S. Census Bureau & HUD via FRED | Analysis by Jordan Blackman",
    y = "Permits Authorized",
    x = "Date"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

p_tslm_fc

# Save image for Canvas upload
ggsave("california_housing_permits_tslm_forecast.png", p_tslm_fc, width = 9, height = 5.5, dpi = 300)
```

```{r plot-ets-forecast}
p_ets_fc <- ca_fc |>
  filter(.model == "ets_auto") |>
  autoplot(tail(ca_trn, 36)) +
  geom_line(data = ca_tst, aes(x = Month, y = permits), color = "black", linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(
    title = "California Housing Permits - ETS(M,Ad,M) Forecast",
    subtitle = "Auto-selected exponential smoothing with multiplicative seasonality and damped trend (Dashed = Actuals)",
    caption = "Source: U.S. Census Bureau & HUD via FRED | Analysis by Jordan Blackman",
    y = "Permits Authorized",
    x = "Date"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

p_ets_fc

# Save image for Canvas upload
ggsave("california_housing_permits_ets_forecast.png", p_ets_fc, width = 9, height = 5.5, dpi = 300)
```

## 8.3 Extended Multi-Year Historical Context (Customizable Training Window)

To view the forecast within a broader macroeconomic context, this plot displays an extended training history. You can adjust the number of preceding training years and select the model (`ets_auto` or `tslm_regime`) using the variables below:

```{r plot-extended-history, fig.width=10, fig.height=5.5}
# ==============================================================================
# USER-CONTROLLED PARAMETERS:
# history_years : Number of years of training history (e.g., 5, 7, 10, 15, 20)
# selected_model: Model to display ("ets_auto", "tslm_regime", "tslm_basic")
# ==============================================================================
history_years  <- 20
selected_model <- "ets_auto"

# Calculate corresponding number of monthly observations
history_months <- history_years * 12

# Model label for titles
model_label <- if (selected_model == "ets_auto") "ETS(M,Ad,M)" else "TSLM"

# Plot Forecast with extended historical training actuals
p_extended_fc <- ca_fc |>
  filter(.model == selected_model) |>
  autoplot(tail(ca_trn, history_months)) +
  geom_line(data = ca_tst, aes(x = Month, y = permits), color = "black", linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(
    title = paste0("California Housing Permits - ", model_label, " Forecast (", history_years, "-Year Training History)"),
    subtitle = paste0("Displaying ", history_years, " years (", history_months, " months) of pre-forecast training actuals alongside holdout test period (Dashed = Actuals)"),
    caption = "Source: U.S. Census Bureau & HUD via FRED | Analysis by Jordan Blackman",
    y = "Permits Authorized",
    x = "Date"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13)
  )

p_extended_fc

# Save high-resolution graphic
output_filename <- paste0("california_housing_permits_", selected_model, "_", history_years, "yr_history.png")
ggsave(output_filename, p_extended_fc, width = 10, height = 5.5, dpi = 300)
message("Saved extended plot to: ", output_filename)
```

# 9. Canvas Discussion 2.1 Post Draft (Exact Exemplar Format)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Data provided by the U.S. Census Bureau and the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (via FRED).**\
The dataset reports monthly new private housing units authorized by building permits from 1988 through 2026. Building permits serve as an officially recognized leading economic indicator for residential construction starts. For this discussion, I've narrowed the analysis to California (`CABPPRIV`), partitioning the series to train on data through December 2023 and evaluate out-of-sample forecasts on 2024–2026.

I attempted a TSLM model so that I could add predictor variables for month of year, secular trend, and a structural break indicator for the post-2008 subprime crisis.

#### Model Parameters

``` text

Model: TSLM 

Residuals:
    Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
-9448.9 -2847.1  -436.6  2066.2 13320.4 

Coefficients:
                  Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
(Intercept)       9188.329    747.576  12.291  < 2e-16 ***
trend()              8.215      2.878   2.854  0.00453 ** 
monthFeb            88.591    908.939   0.097  0.92240    
monthMar          2258.959    908.952   2.485  0.01334 *  
monthApr          2049.549    908.975   2.255  0.02466 *  
monthMay          2308.723    909.007   2.540  0.01145 *  
monthJun          3727.897    909.048   4.101 4.95e-05 ***
monthJul          1457.904    909.098   1.604  0.10954    
monthAug          1855.245    909.158   2.041  0.04192 *  
monthSep           867.557    909.226   0.954  0.34055    
monthOct          1683.137    909.035   1.852  0.06479 .  
monthNov           330.922    909.067   0.364  0.71602    
monthDec          1498.235    909.108   1.648  0.10010    
is_post_2008TRUE -6203.622    726.364  -8.541 2.51e-16 ***
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

Residual standard error: 3856 on 418 degrees of freedom
Multiple R-squared: 0.2997, Adjusted R-squared: 0.2780
F-statistic: 13.76 on 13 and 418 DF, p-value: < 2.22e-16
```

We can see that in June the model predicts over 3,727 additional building permits authorized compared to January, reflecting California's peak summer building season. Additionally, the post-2008 indicator reveals a statistically significant downward level shift of over 6,200 authorized permits per month following the Great Financial Crisis.

*(Attach Plot: `california_housing_permits_tslm_forecast.png`)*

Steps in forecast reflect the month predictor variable in lieu of simple seasonality. Incorporating the 2008 structural break improved test RMSE from 2,094 to 1,169. However, TSLM may not be the best choice for this dataset, and it's worth noting an auto-selected `ETS()` model (`ETS(M,Ad,M)`) performed better than all the TSLM models I tried, achieving a test RMSE of 1,083 and a MAPE of 8.68%.
